messages:
Alex W.: Heads-up: saw ~8% spike of hosted traffic in eu-economy last hour; token spend rose. Proposing routing low-tier requests to 'opt-q4' (4-bit quant) with a per-request token hard cap and short degrade window. Thoughts?
Maya R.: Agree. Can this be purely routing-layer? no client change. Suggest we add opt-in header `x-rw-degrade-allow: true|false` so customers can opt out at client side.
Liam K.: Need numbers. Run the 10k prompt eval to measure quality delta and latency. Also ensure fallback token accounting (regen vs fallback) doesn't double-bill.
Alex W.: Draft plan:
1) routing table keyed by (customer_tier, region) -> variant
2) per-request token_cap + fallback window
3) telemetry: `economy_variant_rate`, `variant_fallback_rate`, `fallback_reason`
Example route config:
```
{"match": {"tier": "economy", "region": "eu"}, "route_to": "opt-q4", "per_request_token_limit": 1200}
```
OpsBot: rollout-bot: scheduled canary deploy to eng-platform ops group at 1819991400 for 15m :rocket:
Maya R.: Console UX: show expected $/1000-token delta per-route, a 'savings vs baseline' column, and a per-customer override toggle. Alerting: `variant_fallback_rate > 2% for 5m`.
Liam K.: API debate: Should fallback be visible? I vote we expose headers: `x-rw-variant: opt-q4` and `x-rw-fallback-reason: capacity|policy|error` so clients can adapt (e.g., reduce tokens or prompt-split).
Product Ops: Customer comms: we need doc snippet + migration guide and clear billing language. Also add example for 'no-fallback' (paid tiers) in API docs.
Alex W.: Implementation details I'll add to RFC: `route_priority` list (economy -> opt-q4 -> opt-q8 -> baseline); greedy token budget to respect SLO; metric names and console mockups.
Maya R.: :thumbsup: please include Dedicated migration notes and a fallback escalation flow (ops alert -> auto-rollback).
SRE-bot: alert: economy_variant_fallback_rate eu > 3.1% (5m) — paging eng-platform @oncall
